solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Playing as well as ever, Labour diva ends up quite relaxed

parts.note: a player at their best is said to be in form

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading the letters from bottom to top, backwards
the ends of a phrase are its first and last letters, so only those two are kept

parts.note: the first letter of Labour and the last letter of diva

explanation.surface: A Labour star singer, back on top form, ends up looking pretty laid-back.
explanation.walkthrough: IN FORM is the sporting phrase for playing at your best. The ends are taken from the two words 'Labour diva' together, L and A, then turned up to give AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal describes a casual, easygoing manner or setting, without stiffness or ceremony.

clue.text: Mate underneath round stone

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting underneath another means it is written after it

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O
a mate is a friend, a pal

explanation.surface: Someone's friend is lying beneath a round boulder.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue names the friend first, but 'underneath' puts it below the round letter in the down light, so O comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Opal is a gemstone with shifting rainbow colours, prized in jewellery as a precious stone.

clue.text: see 25dn.
Sneaking one in, the GP wrongly put a cap on this?

indicators.note: sneaking something in means slipping it inside, so one piece goes into another
done wrongly means put in the wrong order, so these letters must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange
one is the article A

explanation.surface: A doctor sneaks someone in and wrongly caps their bill, or their prescriptions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put a cap on' sounds like setting a limit; the question mark signals the literal reading, hanging a cap on something.
explanation.definitionFit: A hat peg is a wall hook where you hang headgear such as a cap.

clue.text: Kills off official reports

definitions.meaning: first meaning: puts to death quickly
second meaning: formal messages sent back, as from a war front

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as someone burying official reports; the verb and the noun are the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispatch someone is to kill them swiftly, and military or diplomatic despatches are formal written communications.

clue.text: Boris lost charisma ultimately on foreign aid grounds

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so each word gives its final letter

parts.note: the last letters of the three words

indicators.note: something foreign is strange and unfamiliar, so the letters come out in an unfamiliar order

parts.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Boris Johnson's charm finally deserted him over cuts to foreign aid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately' applies to all three words before it. 'Foreign aid' reads as a policy, but 'foreign' scrambles 'aid'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stadia is a plural of stadium, and sports grounds are stadiums where matches are played.

clue.text: Old record kept by courts about Hirst?

indicators.note: what is kept by something is held within it, so one piece goes inside the other
about can mean moved around, so these letters are turned about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange
an LP, long-playing record, is the old vinyl album format

explanation.surface: An old document held by the law courts concerning the artist Damien Hirst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' tempts towards a legal file, but it is a vinyl LP. Damien Hirst is a British artist known for works such as the shark in formaldehyde.
explanation.definitionFit: Hirst makes three-dimensional artworks and installations, so he is an example of a sculptor; the question mark marks the example.

clue.text: Speed is sadly not connected with having an erection

indicators.note: connected with means joined on, so one piece is attached to the next
sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are put in disorder

parts.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange
standing up, erect

explanation.surface: A rueful remark that speed has nothing to do with sexual performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not connected' reads as one phrase, but 'not' is the fodder and 'connected with' the join. A ton is British slang for 100 miles per hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Ton-up describes doing a hundred miles an hour, especially on a motorbike, so it is a phrase for high speed.

clue.text: Boob by chaplain, a small one

parts.note: slang for a breast
CH is the abbreviation for chaplain

explanation.surface: A clergyman's blunder, and only a minor one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boob' reads as a mistake, its other meaning; here it is the body part. Titch is British slang for a small person.
explanation.definitionFit: Titch is an informal British nickname for a very small person or child.

clue.text: Practical application of elastic to bind one after end of knee-trembler

indicators.note: after means following, so the earlier piece in the clue is written later
the end of a word is its last letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

indicators.note: to bind is to tie around, so one piece wraps another
an application puts material to new use, so these letters are reworked into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A practical use for elastic during a knee-trembler, British slang for sex while standing up.
explanation.walkthrough: The scrambled elastic holds the I, and the whole lot comes after R.
explanation.definitionFit: Being realistic means taking a sensible, down-to-earth view, so it is a synonym for practical.

clue.text: Unreasonably led, spilling seed — I'll be off

parts.note: too means excessively, beyond what is reasonable

indicators.note: spilling scatters things all over, so these letters land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange
a pip is a small fruit seed

explanation.surface: Someone unreasonably led on, having spilled their seed, makes a hasty exit.
explanation.walkthrough: Toodle-pip is old-fashioned British slang for goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Toodle-pip is a jaunty farewell, said by someone announcing that they are leaving now.

clue.text: Hack into China? On yer bike!

indicators.note: going into something means ending up inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: rhyming slang: china plate means mate, a pal
a hack is a journalist; ED is short for editor, another newspaper person

explanation.surface: A cyber attack on China is met with a curt dismissal: get lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack into' suggests computer intrusion, but 'Hack' is a newsman and 'into' the container. On yer bike is a British brush-off meaning go away.
explanation.definitionFit: The order to pedal, push the cranks round, is literally what 'on yer bike' tells a cyclist to do.

clue.text: (&14ac.) The government plans to diminish this migrant cash transaction (to be confined in small, basic building)

definitions.text: The government plans to diminish this

indicators.note: being confined in a place means being shut up inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a hut is a small, simple shelter

indicators.note: a transaction trades things around, so these letters change places

parts.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange
taken as written, as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A satire on government migration policy, with migrants' money changing hands and people housed in crude shelters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Migrant cash transaction' reads as a payment, but the last word stirs the first two. The Human Rights Act 1998 is the UK law that some ministers wanted to scrap or water down.
explanation.definitionFit: The UK government at the time proposed replacing or weakening the 1998 statute protecting rights, so this law is what it planned to diminish.

clue.text: Barnier? A reign too involved with Brexit at the end

indicators.note: involved means tangled and complicated, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange

indicators.note: at the end points to the final letter of the word, which alone is kept

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Michel Barnier seemingly ruled over Brexit for far too long at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Michel Barnier led the European Union's side in the Brexit talks.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnier was the EU's chief Brexit negotiator, so he is an example of one; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: see 13ac.
Go down on former spy, being a sucker

parts.note: to fall is to go down
Guy Burgess, one of the Cambridge spies who defected to Moscow

explanation.surface: A crude innuendo about a spy's sexual tastes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go down on' reads as a sexual act; 'on' just joins the pieces in an across clue. Guy Burgess was a British diplomat who spied for the Soviet Union.
explanation.definitionFit: A fall guy is a dupe who takes the blame for others, an easily fooled victim or sucker.

clue.text: Blow job machine act is adapted for extremists

parts.note: a fan is a machine whose job is to blow air

indicators.note: something adapted has been altered to fit, so these letters are changed in order

parts.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A rude-sounding sex aid modified for people with extreme tastes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow job' is innuendo; read straight, a machine whose job is to blow is a fan.
explanation.definitionFit: Fanatics hold zealous, uncompromising views, which makes them synonyms for extremists.

clue.text: To do with the Sun crushing church academic

indicators.note: crushing something means squeezing it in tight, so one piece is pressed inside another

parts.note: solar means relating to the sun
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: The Sun tabloid flattening a churchman with academic pretensions.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital S makes 'the Sun' look like the newspaper, but it is the star, giving the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar is a learned person who studies a subject deeply, which is what an academic is.

clue.text: Tabloid grilled Brown?

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
food grilled too long ends up burnt

explanation.surface: A tabloid gave Gordon Brown, the former Labour Prime Minister, a roasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grilled' reads as interrogated and 'Brown' as the politician; the question mark warns that it is the colour of skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin that has been sunburnt is often tanned or reddened, so brown is a loose description of it.

clue.text: It's only right for a member to get turned on in the extremes of agony

definitions.note: a phrase standing for the noun: what is lawful

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece is placed within the other
the extremes are the two outermost points, so only the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
a lamp turned on is lit

explanation.surface: A naughty suggestion that it's only fair a man gets aroused even when in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' and 'turned on' carry innuendo; they are a limb and a lit lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Legality is the quality of being lawful, and what the law allows is what is officially right.

clue.text: Retiring person's habit of playing with thing (good, admit)

indicators.note: playing with something means fiddling with it, so these letters are moved about

parts.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange
G is the abbreviation for good
to own up is to admit, so own means admit

explanation.surface: A shy person confesses to a fondness for playing with their thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' reads as shy and 'habit' as a custom; together they mean what someone going to bed wears.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit can be a garment, as a monk's is, and someone retiring for the night wears nightclothes.

clue.text: Try taking on knockers and lose all your money

indicators.note: taking something on means adding it, so a second piece is joined after the first

parts.note: to have a go is to try
knockers is slang for breasts, a bust

explanation.surface: A gambler takes on a buxom rival and ends up broke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knockers' could mean critics, but here it is slang for a woman's chest.
explanation.definitionFit: To go bust is an informal phrase for becoming bankrupt, having no money left.

clue.text: Spectacular bloomer has love child moving right not left

indicators.note: moving one way and not the other swaps the left-hand letter out for the right-hand one

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A spectacular blunder: a love child is involved, and someone shifts politically from left to right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' reads as a gaffe but means a flower. L for left leaves 'child' and R for right comes in, placed at its head.
explanation.definitionFit: Orchids are flowering plants famed for their showy, exotic blooms.

clue.text: Taunt American making a U-turn for a sweetener

indicators.note: a U-turn goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to rag is to tease or taunt
US is short for American

explanation.surface: Mocking an American politician for a policy U-turn made in exchange for a bribe.
explanation.walkthrough: The U-turn applies to both pieces together.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar is the standard substance added to food and drink to make them taste sweet.

clue.text: Crafty sportsperson, argumentative type

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an oarsman, whose sport uses a boat, a craft
second meaning: someone who rows, rhyming with cows, meaning quarrels

explanation.walkthrough: 'Crafty' suggests cunning but means using a craft, a boat. The two meanings are pronounced differently.
explanation.definitionFit: One meaning is an athlete who propels a boat with oars; the other is someone forever starting quarrels.

clue.text: A small piece folded back over one's bony member

indicators.note: folding something back turns it the other way, so the letters run backwards
folded over something means wrapped around it, so those letters end up enclosed by the rest

parts.note: taken as written
a bit is a small piece
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A little flap of something folded back over a man's private part.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition; 'member' is a limb, not the innuendo.
explanation.definitionFit: The tibia is the shinbone, a bone in the lower leg, which is a limb or member of the body.

clue.text: Particularly hard setback caused by raw cannabis

parts.note: raw, as in a raw deal, means harsh or cruel
blow is a slang name for cannabis

explanation.surface: Someone suffers a nasty setback after smoking strong unprocessed weed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raw cannabis' reads as one phrase, but the adjective and the drug are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruel blow is an idiom for a harsh misfortune or disappointing reverse.

clue.text: (& 3dn.) "Abandoned right by gutless politician," as an owner might claim

definitions.note: the thing an owner claims, not a verb phrase

indicators.note: without guts means with the inside removed, so only the outer letters stay

parts.note: something abandoned is gone, mislaid
proper means right, correct
a Tory politician, emptied of its middle letters

explanation.surface: A gutless politician leaves something behind, and its owner declares it was abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory is the everyday name for a British Conservative. The definition works as a cryptic hint: owners claim back their things from a lost property office.
explanation.definitionFit: Lost property is the mislaid items handed in for their rightful owners to collect, which is something an owner claims.

clue.text: Conservative type organised a discount

indicators.note: organised means put into order, so these letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A Tory type has fixed up a bargain price for himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conservative' with a capital looks political, but it means someone who conserves.
explanation.definitionFit: A custodian is a keeper who looks after and preserves something, a guardian who conserves it.

clue.text: Lecherous male rested a short time

parts.note: to sit down is to rest
YR is the shortened form of year, a span of time

explanation.surface: A randy man took a brief breather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A short time' reads as a brief while, but it is a unit of time cut short to its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A satyr is a lustful woodland creature from Greek myth, and by extension a lustful man.
